biggest_gap.what: A spell does not connect with anything that moves. A LIGHT-class bolt fired at a body 18 m away deals 80 damage when the body is stationary and 0 damage the moment it moves laterally at 1.5 m/s - slower than the walk speed measured in the same arena, 3.17 m/s - and 0 at 3, 5 and 7 m/s. spell_impact fires in every row; effect_apply fires only at 0 m/s. This is not the tracking fence: AP-M3 passes cleanly under an instrument that re-derives the turn rate from consecutive headings (LIGHT 60.00 dps before the fence and 0.00 after, 0 violating frames, --break=nocutoff red at 72 frames), and the arc is real at 21.95 deg on LIGHT and 24.16 deg on HEAVY. The bolt steers and still misses, because it steers toward the position it acquired at release rather than the position the target now occupies, and the 0.35 x journey fence closes before the error is paid off. The comparison that rules out an instrument artefact is touch range, measured the same way with the same setEntityPos calls: a retreating body takes full damage at 0 and 1 m/s and none at 3, so the harness demonstrably drives the same resolver.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Every enemy in this build repositions - the arena's own bodies sit in REPOSITION for the whole of a 900-frame observation - so the offensive half of the catalogue, which is every projectile- and target-range effect and therefore all five damage effects and most of the status verbs, does not work against a live opponent at all. It also explains a structural fact about every census this piece has ever run, mine included: they all pin a body at 1.4 m and use touch range, because that is the only geometry that connects. DISTINCT-VERBS 53/55 is a true statement about a build in which the thing a player actually does with a spell in a fight does not land. And it is the round's own new protocol rule - if the thing being measured responds to motion, the target must move - applied to the one place the round that wrote it did not apply it.

remedy.action: In sim/magic/system.js's projectile step, re-acquire the target's current position on every frame the projectile is inside its tracking window instead of latching the aim point at release, and derive the cutoff from the predicted intercept rather than from the acquisition-time journey.
remedy.acceptance: A LIGHT bolt fired at a body 18 m away strafing at 1.5, 3 and 5 m/s deals its full deterministic damage in at least 2 of the 3 rows, measured in headless Chromium with tools/harness/critic-w1-14-r3-motion.mjs; AND AP-M3 still reports 0 violating frames past 0.35 x travel_f on LIGHT, HEAVY and CANTRIP; AND __breakTrackingCutoff() still drives the violating-frame count above 50 on LIGHT.

secondary_observations.what: THE CAMERA OVERRIDE IS NOT BROKEN, AND THIS MATTERS BEYOND MAGIC. The round-3 builder reported RI-MAG05 as blocked because H.camera({pos,look,fov}) 'is NOT taking effect - every frame is shot from the default follow rig'. Measured from four sides: readback is exact immediately and after 24 steps; the override survives a full spell cast unchanged; loadState clears it, correctly; and the pixels change 96.94% between the builder's own pose and the default rig, 96.08% for a 40 m-high fov-20 pose and 99.999% for a pose looking the other way. stepCamera short-circuits to applyOverride and renderer.render reads sim.camera.pos/pivot/fov directly. There is no regression to escalate and RI-MAG05 was judgeable all along; with a framing I chose the impact peak changes 15.36% of the frame rather than the 0.083% the builder reported.

ENEMY CASTERS DO NOT EXIST, ON ANY ARCHETYPE, FOR THE THIRD ROUND. cst_sap_speaker, champion_hist_marked, drowned_greater, drowned_lesser, guard_legion, beast_slitherfang, cam_boss_great, cam_boss_mid, cam_elite and inf_trash, each aggroed for 900 frames: zero cast events, zero magic events, zero player damage, on all ten. RI-MAG01 M7 is 10 of 100 weight and five of the item's six magic anti-patterns cannot be measured without one. Round 1 found it; rounds 2 and 3 did not touch it.

THE ENEMY NEVER ATTACKS IN THIS ARENA EITHER. Across three independent probes an aggroed body at 1.2-1.6 m left the player on full health for 600-900 frames. That is a W1-09/W1-12 matter rather than this piece's, but it is also why S29's 300-frame post-hostile clause could not be armed: sim.lastHostileFrame is stamped only from bus HOSTILE_EVENTS in sim/step.js:45, H.damagePlayer() emits none of them, and no arena I could build produced a real one. The builder's demonstration of that clause used damagePlayer() and was therefore measuring inCombat.

THE UTILITY VERBS' WORLD IS A FIXTURE. game/data/magic/wards.json carries its own _placement_note: 'Coordinates are inside arena_flat, within the reach declared in WORLD_REACH_M of a spell cast forward from the origin.' Every lock, trap, breakable, key and shrine open_lock, lock_lock, ward_trap, shatter and detect_key act on is placed inside the probe's arena. There is not one of them in helstrom-market, stormhold-street, writ-house or rootlands-well-graph.

CALM_BEAST, DEMORALISE AND CHARM ARE ONE VERB. With a beast_slitherfang pinned at 1.3 m and 720 frames of observation, all three deliver, all three set yielded, all three end in_combat, and all three leave the body at 0.00 m displacement. Demoralise does not flee. The builder admitted a two-way collision; it is three-way.

THE BINDS ARE NOT IDENTICAL, THEY ARE MAGNITUDE-BLIND. bind_lesser summons INFANTRY hp 260 at magnitude 1 AND at 90; bind_greater summons hp 640 at magnitude 1 and is refused at 90. So the two differ in the thing they summon, contrary to the builder's note, and both ignore magnitude.

h_fortify_skill IGNORES THE SCHOOL IT COMPUTES. apply.js:219 sets `const which = rec.school || 'warding'` and never reads it; the loop adds the magnitude to all four entries of M.skillFortify and to stealth security and sneak. One fortify_skill cast fortifies everything. It is not a gate leak - fortify_skill's own min_tier forces skill_req 45, so a starting character cannot attune it - but it is a magnitude applied four times over.

FROSTBITE IS NOT CONSUMED, against the builder's 5/5 claim. Treatment vs an identical control on the same spawned body over 180 frames: fire, shock, poison and paralysis all differ; the frostbite row is byte-identical, including stamina_max, move_speed_mult and the frostbitten flag.

CASTING IS SILENT. getStealthState().sound_r_m is 0 on every casting frame and an enemy at 18 m or 30 m stays IDLE through a full cast and a bolt that lands beside it. Only the body at 8 m reacts, and by sight. A spell is the loudest thing a Morrowind mage does.

takeProp() DOES NOT CHECK reach_m. The harness's own take verb sets o.taken = true unconditionally, while the real interact press at engine.js:1500 does gate on the prop's reach_m. My first consumption pass used takeProp() and wrongly read telekinesis as a no-op; the correction is recorded here because any probe using takeProp() to test reach is measuring nothing. A harness note for W1-00, not a magic defect.

THE TREE DOES NOT BOOT AT HEAD. game/data/input/profiles.json, added by commit 12be950, violates its own RI-JRN04 H11 assertion twice: heavy/parry are 6.9 px apart and block/roll 0.11 px apart against an 8 px minimum, so TouchInput._assertLayout throws before window.__HARNESS ever appears. Every probe in the project that boots the engine is blocked by it. smoke.mjs passes because it never boots the engine, which is worth fixing on its own.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-MAG06 section E/M8 says 'any effect, spell or resolution that is reachable only with the [gating] call is unmeasurable => 0 on the item it serves'. The builder's census arena reaches skill 100 through 2,800 grantSkillUse calls, and 25 of 55 effects are uncastable without it. But I measured that a player reaches sorcery 100 in 673 real casts, so those effects are reachable by playing - just deep in the ladder. Does M8's zero bite on a gate a player CAN climb, or only on one they cannot? I have not zeroed them; I have scored the arena-audit axis at its own 6 band (hand-set, and the census re-run without it) and published both numbers.
sides: The letter of M8 is about reachability through the harness call, and skill 100 is reachable without it, so the effects are measurable and the zero does not apply.

The spirit of section E is that a probe must not measure a state the shipped game does not put the player in on day one; 17/72 at creation against 55/55 in the census is exactly the gap the section was written to expose, and publishing only the maxed number is the failure it names.
arbitration_questions.recommendation: Amend M8 to require BOTH numbers - the census at the shipped starting sheet and at the reachable ceiling - and to make the arena-audit axis 10 only when both are published. That keeps the zero for genuinely unreachable states and stops a maxed census being reported as the number.

arbitration_questions.question: S29 has two clauses and only one is testable. The in-combat clause is enforced and demonstrable. The 300-frames-after-the-last-hostile-action clause reads sim.lastHostileFrame, which sim/step.js:45 stamps only from bus HOSTILE_EVENTS - and no harness surface emits one. H.damagePlayer() does not, so the builder's demonstration of the clause was measuring inCombat; and in this build an aggroed enemy does not attack, so no arena produces a real one either. Should a seam ruling whose second clause has no reachable test be scored as enforced, as unmeasured, or as a harness debt?
sides: The code is present and correct-looking and the first clause demonstrably works, so scoring it as unenforced would be a fabrication.
SCORING 1.1 fixes unmeasurable at 0 fail-closed, and 'the code looks right' is exactly the reasoning CRITIC-DOCTRINE 1.1 forbids.
arbitration_questions.recommendation: Record it as unmeasured (which I have) and add a harness surface that stamps sim.lastHostileFrame the way a real swing does - or expose the field for reading - so the clause becomes testable before it is scored either way.
